In a recent resolution passed after a joint extraordinary general body meeting held on August 5, the bar bodies said Kumar had made generalised statements claiming that bar associations have failed to protect women lawyers and provide them a safe environment . Over 400 advocates attended the meeting. “Resolved that the name of Shri Amit Kumar be and is hereby removed from the roll of advocates of both the High Court of Meghalaya Bar Association and the Shillong Bar Association and he shall no longer be a member of the said Associations, and it [is] hereby resolved that all members of the both the bar associations henceforth do not recognize Shri Amit Kumar as Advocate General for the State of Meghalaya," the resolution said. items.title: How far does reputation of a famous family name extend? Delhi HC asks in Aaradhya Bachchan case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday framed several key legal questions that it will examine in a suit filed by Aaradhya Bachchan, the granddaughter of actor Amitabh Bachchan, against the circulation of misleading information about her on the internet. Among other queries, Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani has raised a question of how far the reputation attached to a famous family name can extend across generations. "The value of trademark and reputation in the trademark arises from the fact that a product or service is service has been rendered. Now, this is somewhat contextually different when you are talking about a person. A certain last name has a reputation because of the achievements, the eminence in a certain field of work, etc. So, does that reputation - you are couching it as virtually as a trademark - does that flow down generationally? items.title: Will provide rail travel concessions for acid attack survivors: Centre to Supreme Court
items.summary: The Central government told the Supreme Court on Thursday that it has agreed in principle to formulate a policy granting railway travel concessions to acid attack survivors, particularly to help them travel for medical treatment. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a plea by Atijeevan Society seeking railway concessions and reservation benefits for acid attack survivors. CJI Kant pointed out that acid attack survivors are already recognised as persons with disabilities under the law. He noted that the issue could be addressed as part of a social welfare measure. "Putting them in the disabled category, that has now been statutorily resolved, with the amendment through another petition before us," he said. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana Additional Solicitor General Archana Pathak Dave submitted that the Centre is proposing to extend the concession under the existing “patient category”, rather than create a separate concession under the disability category. items.title: Tamil Nadu: Nine-year-old girl allegedly sexually assaulted while walking home
items.summary: A nine-year-old Class 4 student was allegedly sexually assaulted by an unidentified man while she was walking home in Denkanikottai in Tamil Nadu’s Krishnagiri district on the evening of August 12, Wednesday. The child was walking home with three other children, but the three reached their homes before her, leaving her alone when the alleged assault took place, according to police. The incident was reported around 1 am on Thursday after the child’s mother lodged a complaint with the Denkanikottai All Women Police Station (AWPS). Police have registered an FIR under Section 87 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) (kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc) and Section 5(6) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The child was taken to Krishnagiri Government Hospital for a medical examination. Police said the examination will help determine whether a sexual assault took place. A police team has also visited the scene and is collecting evidence and other information as part of the investigation. The child does not know the identity of the alleged accused, but has told police that she would be able to identify him.
